headline: Backup Power for Travis County Homes
summary: Travis County has a moderate outlook. It sees a long outage of 12 hours or more about once every 11 years. This comes from 8 years of records since 2018. In February 2021, 43% of homes in the county lost power. The longest-waiting tenth went about 74 hours without power. In February 2023, 29% of homes in the county lost power. The longest-waiting tenth went about 106 hours without power. One Core lasts about 18 hours in August. One Core lasts about 44 hours in February. Two Cores last about 34 hours in August. Two Cores cover 93% of past 12-hour-plus outage hours. Base confirms sizing at install.
